limitations: The isolated producer fixtures test real engine growth, candidate/control causality, owner-requested application/rollback and measured automatic acceptance or rejection. A regional-growth stress proposal may fail the unchanged default utility threshold; rejection is retained rather than relabeled as successful intervention. These fixtures contain no humans/animals and cannot establish human learning or population balance.

Full-world automatic probes accelerate Cardinal observation/history/experiment scheduling and use 30-second (0.2-game-hour) candidate horizons. The isolated automatic producer fixture retains the normal900-second horizon and normal0.01 acceptance threshold, with accelerated initial observation scheduling only. Neither establishes reliable long-term biological optimization.
Automatic live and shadow probes use a documented0.25-second timestep. The distribution/performance probe uses the native1/60-second timestep, but does not measure rendering or native UI latency.
Held-out seeds change future choices/weather at the same saved geometry and checkpoint; they are not independently generated worlds.
Only two default starting seeds and short windows are functional evidence. Long-term self-sufficiency, ecological balance, optimal policies and civilization development are unestablished.
Cardinal utility, diagnostics, candidate rules and safeguards are supplied structure. Persisted utility estimates affect candidate selection; no model weights or general world model are learned.
The evaluator supplies no food technique, human answer or live model. Human physiology, knowledge and inventories are outside the world-rule actuator boundary.
Original v0.6 discovery/ecological runs remain historical evidence and are not silently relabeled as tests of this Cardinal release.
